<strong>Con dos lados y un ángulo, cosen: With two sides and an angle, the cosine rule; with two angles and a side, the sine rule. Choosing the theorem from the data and not from habit halves the time spent on triangle problems.
<strong>Dibuja la circunferencia antes d: Draw the circle before deciding the sign. An angle placed in its quadrant answers by itself whether the cosine is negative or the sine positive. Memorising the table of signs fails; the drawing does not.
<strong>Trabaja en radianes si aparece u: Work in radians if a function appears. The derivatives and the waves of the rest of the course are in radians, and mixing units halfway through a problem is the costliest mistake in the block.
<strong>Una ecuación trigonométrica tien: A trigonometric equation has infinitely many solutions. Give the general one, with its period, and then narrow it to the interval the question asks for. Giving only the first-quadrant one leaves half the exercise undone.
Cada tramo aporta un número fijo de preg: Each section contributes a fixed number of questions, drawn at random from its topics without repeating a topic while that is possible, and avoiding the most basic exercises. With 5 topics and 6 questions, one exam covers almost the whole block: that is why the link at the end reproduces the same exam, and “another exam” draws a different one.
Cinco temas que convierten ángulos en lo: Five topics that turn angles into lengths and end in a wave that repeats. This topic teaches nothing new: it asks. A procedural exam with exercises from the whole block, with a clock and no hints, because what is here comes back in [[fn-derivadas|derivatives]], in [[av-fourier|Fourier]] and in every sound of the synthesis block.
Cómo sacarle partido: How to get the most out of it
El enlace de un examen corregido reprodu: The link to a marked exam reproduces the same questions with the same numbers. A teacher can do one, copy the link and pass it to the class: everyone will sit the same exam and will be able to compare results and procedures.
El seno de $-30°$ es $-1/2$, no $1/2$: e: The sine of $-30°$ is $-1/2$, not $1/2$: sine is an odd function. The second solution is in the second quadrant, at $150°$.
El seno vale lo mismo en dos cuadrantes,: The sine takes the same value in two quadrants, and the function repeats every $360°$. The complete answer is $x = 30° + 360°k$ and $x = 150° + 360°k$.
Elige los tramos que entran. Las pregunt: Choose the sections to include. The questions are drawn at random from the exercises of each topic in the block, avoiding the most basic ones and without repeating a topic while possible. There are no hints: the marking and the step-by-step solution come on submitting.
Es <em>un</em> ángulo, no el único. La c: It is an angle, not the only one. The calculator returns one because it has to return something; the equation has infinitely many.
Las primeras tablas trigonométricas se h: The first trigonometric tables were made to examine the sky, not students: Hipparchus of Nicaea tabulated chords around 150 BCE to predict the positions of heavenly bodies, and Ptolemy carried the work on. For fifteen hundred years, knowing trigonometry meant knowing how to use a table; today the table is in the calculator and what is examined is what the table cannot do: choosing the ratio, the quadrant and the theorem.

Seno, coseno y tangente en un triángulo: Sine, cosine and tangent in a right-angled triangle; converting degrees to radians; the sign of each ratio by quadrant; reducing an angle to the first quadrant.
Sí: $30°$ es el ángulo cuyo seno es $1/2: Yes: $30°$ is the angle whose sine is $1/2$
Un examen de bloque es un simulacro hech: A block exam is a mock paper taken at home: with a clock, no notes and no hints. The questions come from the exercises of the 5 topics of the block, spread across sections, and every time you start one the numbers are different and so are the topics: doing it several times covers the whole block. On submission everything is marked, the step-by-step solution of each question opens, and the mark comes out section by section, with links to what is worth revising. The “tailored to what you have done” option puts first what you have not solved yet: it is the way to check that no topic is left untouched.
Usar la identidad fundamental y las del: Using the fundamental identity and the double-angle ones; solving a trigonometric equation giving every solution; applying the sine or the cosine rule according to the data; reading amplitude, period and phase from a sinusoid.
